title: Investigate perceived hang during Hybrid suspend-to-hibernate
description: User reports machine seemed stuck, held/pressed power to force off, then startup returned to same session. PowerDevil requested s2h at 22:12:07; suspend at 22:12:08; timer wake 22:42:10; late graphics preflight complete Hybrid/attached/settled with expected active desktop clients; hibernate starts 22:42:11.338565 at monotonic 13933.684028; return 22:45:56.504606 at monotonic 13957.631432. Realtime gap 225.166s minus monotonic 23.947s gives about 201.219 seconds outside monotonic execution, strongly supporting hibernation-image restore rather than a cold boot. Kernel records Normal pages needed, device restore and hibernation exit; no explicit restored-image line was captured (PM debug may be off). Service reports success and thaws users at 22:45:59. Only existing DrKonqi failed unit remains. Wi-Fi restore -110 recurs (lllf-j9t.6.5); post hook rejects legitimate Hybrid clients separately. Cannot determine from logs alone whether a real hang occurred or exactly what the power button did. Await screen state, press duration and approximate event time from user; do not attribute incident to undeployed next-boot code.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve timeline and user context; determine black sleep/off screen vs frozen desktop or boot stall and short press vs forced-off hold. Correlate source kernel timestamps, sleep logs and failed-unit delta; identify a specific failure only with evidence. No repeat forced-off experiment or new sleep/graphics transition without explicit recovery plan.
notes:
User clarification: keyboard and power-button lights were still on when the machine seemed stuck. This establishes observed LEDs only; it does not by itself distinguish suspend, in-progress hibernation, or a hang. Screen state, whether LEDs actually went out during a held power press, and exact event time are still unknown. Deployment remains paused pending clarification.
Further user clarification: screen was dark (not a reported visible frozen desktop), with keyboard/power-button LEDs on. This is consistent with the logged suspend/hibernate interval but does not rule out a wake issue; whether a long press extinguished LEDs is still unconfirmed. Do not mark the incident resolved. Continued only low-risk boot-setup preparation under the user's proceed instruction; no live activation, graphics selection, sudo or reboot initiated by the agent.

Captured full compositor window privately as kwin-resume.log in the same incident directory. Do NOT dismiss the reported dark-screen hang based on systemd Result=success or empty failed-unit lists. Important user clarification: 'its like hibernation completes but parts of the computer stay on'. Refocus investigation on possible final hibernation power-off failure (image saved, machine not fully off), not solely display wake or immediate re-suspend. A saved image can restore after a forced power cut; unchanged boot/session and systemd return-success therefore do not prove the earlier physical power-off completed. Still need distinguish fans/heat/actual active hardware from standby keyboard/power LEDs and establish duration from user's past observation. Do not request another uninstrumented forced-off reproduction. Pending graphics request cancellation is verified phase cancelled; current Hybrid baseline stays unchanged.
User is unsure whether fans remained running. Do not turn this uncertainty into confirmation of either a kernel power-off hang or normal standby lighting. title: Design guarded next-boot graphics selection and startup gating
description: Read-only audit 2026-11-03: packaging/nixos/legion-telemetry.nix:216-257 defines legion-graphics-reconcile.service, required and ordered before display-manager, ordered before NVIDIA CDI, with lifecycle cleanup as ExecStartPost. Deployed PID1 properties match. Boot 3a1b0a31 journal at 16:59:34-36 records complete zero-client Hybrid/attached/settled, not an iGPU-only transition. Reconciler restores firmware-selected policy only; deployed legion.py GraphicsModeFeature.reconcile does not select a requested next-boot mode. Existing tool/deploy_igpu_boot_order_tty.sh requires iGPU-only already selected. There is no explicit ordering/requirement gate on systemd-user-sessions.service or user@.service, so early login/lingering user services are not covered by the display-manager gate (current prnice Linger=no is only a host observation). Normal host NVIDIA config loads nvidia in initrd. Host no-nvidia specialisation uses legacy activation-time hybrid-mode-enable and PCI remove udev rules; it is not a substitute for the guarded firmware policy. User requested investigation of a deterministic boot-time alternative; no authorization yet to implement startup behavior changes, deploy, or reboot. Proposed next work: an explicit opt-in next-boot request applied only during boot, a reviewed startup gate for user sessions/managers and GPU-capable system consumers, complete root inspection immediately before action, authoritative topology/module cleanup verification, bounded failure and logged recovery. No scan/order graph alone should be described as a global device-open exclusion barrier.
acceptance_criteria: Agree desired-mode request lifetime, activation-vs-real-boot behavior, trusted consumer scope, device-open race limits, and recovery before implementation. Mock unexpected-client and inspection failures and prove no unsafe write; test cleanup failure propagation, stale request handling, no live application during rebuild, no automatic retry after reboot failure, and normal Hybrid behavior. Evaluate rendered Nix graph and systemd ordering (including user managers and CDI/Docker) for cycles; full host build before user-triggered boot validation. Do not bypass driver guards, force unload/detach, use raw PCI removal, or claim arbitrary-process race freedom without an enforced access barrier.
notes: Implemented opt-in nextBootGraphics after user approval. Added typed Polkit-authorized RequestGraphicsModeAtBoot/CancelGraphicsModeAtBoot/GetGraphicsBootRequest and same-connection terminal client; fixed immutable helper handles private atomic/fsynced state with originating boot ID, 24h expiry, before-action consumption, and failed/interrupted-attempt lockout until explicit recovery. No live hardware action during queue/cancel/status or post-boot service activation. Boot checks running user managers, root clients, supported existing Hybrid policy, internal/external displays; uses guarded backend selection, reconciliation, cleanup, fresh final status. Added user-session/manager and known container/NVIDIA startup ordering, CDI success requirement, console recovery, and restartIfChanged=false for reconcile to avoid restarting its display-manager dependency on live rebuild. Tests: 17 Python transition tests; native package CTest 3/3 including real dispatcher and desktop client on private bus with simulated authorization; installed --help; existing lifecycle/CDI/reconcile-loop suites and 13 TTY tests; Nixfmt/clang-format/diff checks; disabled-default and required-option Nix evaluations. title: Prevent NVIDIA CDI regeneration from blocking iGPU-only hibernate resume
description: Normal graphical-session hibernate restored the same boot and desktop/audio, but the NVIDIA udev rule restarted nvidia-container-toolkit-cdi-generator.service while user.slice was frozen. Its nvidia-ctk process held NVIDIA devices at the second reconciliation attempt, causing the hook to reject clients and thaw with NVIDIA attached. The current ExecCondition checks only PCI presence and passes during transient resume re-enumeration. Gate CDI generation on authoritative expected attached policy as well as NVIDIA PCI presence; retain strict reconciliation client rejection.

title: Guard suspend-then-hibernate with authoritative detached graphics preflight
description: The pending lifecycle preflight is ordered before systemd-hibernate.service only. The configured lid path uses systemd-suspend-then-hibernate.service, which bypasses that guard even though the post hook handles its hibernate phase. Design and validate a guard sufficiently close to the actual hibernate transition; a check only before the initial suspend may become stale. Keep this path outside the direct-hibernate validation claim.
notes:
2026-09-09 deployment verified on the running system (generation a83lrj7pxxhjdvpvkdhhha07zkk2b4ci, 20260908.d6524aa). The suspend-then-hibernate drop-in overrides ExecStart with the patched f7sif91nk1vk3zfial5j13km478i7hbp-legion-systemd-sleep-261.2, which embeds the djn4zffj6fzgipfhzdgs5ia0j7vvsdr2 preflight wrapper. The preflight is Before and required by both systemd-hibernate.service and systemd-suspend-then-hibernate.service. The rendered wrapper passes its real timeout/exit-propagation test. Authoritative user-run root status: complete inspection, zero clients, detached/settled. System running with zero failed units and unchanged shutdown-mode sleep config. Hardware validation of the s2h path remains pending: manual-wake-before-delay test first, then a timer-driven hibernate transition with journal evidence and post-resume graphics/desktop/audio/Wi-Fi verification.
2026-09-09 root cause found for suspend-then-hibernate never sleeping: hosts/nixos/hardware/hibernate.nix defined empty nvidia-suspend/nvidia-resume ordering shims (no ExecStart) with requiredBy/wantedBy on systemd-suspend-then-hibernate.service. systemd 261.2 refuses empty services (Service has no ExecStart=, ExecStop=, or SuccessAction=. Refusing), so each s2h job failed with 'Unit nvidia-suspend.service has a bad unit file setting' before any suspend. Direct suspend and hibernate were unaffected because they do not require that unit. With NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1 (open modules + 595 default) these units are ordering-only, so both now use Type=oneshot with ExecStart=coreutils true. Host build passed (vlxsalhsphhyf67ddpw22jmd6b0xlqjl) with the valid units and preserved s2h requires symlinks. One normal-suspend attempt also hit a transient EBUSY right after wlo1 deauthentication (mt7921e in-flight state); a retry succeeded. Hardware validation pending user switch and retest.
2026-09-09 manual-wake validation PASSED at monotonic 129776-129782 after switch deployed the no-op nvidia-suspend fix: nvidia-suspend.service started and deactivated successfully, entry preflight reported complete zero-client detached/settled inspection, system suspended ~1s, user woke manually, no hibernate attempt occurred (correct for wake before HibernateDelaySec), user.slice thawed, service finished with zero failed units, and graphics remains detached/settled. Remaining: timer-driven transition test (30-minute delay or a temporary shortened HibernateDelaySec reverted afterward) to validate the second preflight between suspend return and hibernate write, followed by same-image restore verification.
close_reason: Manual-wake and timer-driven suspend-then-hibernate cycles both validated after the nvidia-suspend no-op fix: entry preflight, patched-binary second preflight between suspend return and hibernate write, same-image restore (boot a4af09f3), post-resume reconciliation to detached/settled with complete zero-client inspection before user.slice thaw, desktop/audio/Wi-Fi recovered automatically, zero failed units, sleep config and PM diagnostics restored. title: Reconcile dGPU after iGPU-only hibernate resume
description: Shutdown-mode hibernation from settled hybrid-igpu-only successfully wrote and restored the same kernel image, but firmware/hardware reset made the NVIDIA PCI functions reappear during kernel device restoration. Read-only ACPI analysis identifies the platform-S4 trigger. DSDT GPP0._PRW advertises GPE 0x08 for S4 wake when WKPM=1, matching enabled /proc/acpi/wakeup node pci:0000:00:01.1. Global _PTS handles Arg0=4 by calling DGHP(One). DGHP sets dGPU-present state, invokes GPP0.PG00._ON, waits 100ms, and notifies PEGP with a bus check. PG00._ON performs physical dGPU power-on and waits for NVIDIA vendor 0x10de. Linux acpi_hibernation_ops.pre_snapshot executes this ACPI preparation before create_image() checks pm_wakeup_pending(). Both failures then log GPP0 Card present, Link Up, and spurious PME with no competing S4 wake-device event. The exact wakeup-source object/IRQ was not printed because pm_debug_messages=0, but firmware-induced GPP0 hotplug is established as the rollback trigger. First workaround candidate: systemd HibernateMode=shutdown, which bypasses platform pre-snapshot callbacks and _PTS(4); unvalidated. Do not disable GPP0 wake first because firmware would still power on the dGPU during frozen topology. Do not retry platform mode. Any shutdown-mode test must first enable pm_debug_messages and pm_print_times and prepare immediate root capture of wakeup_sources, pm_wakeup_irq, graphics topology, and journal if it returns.
Prepared a fail-closed shutdown-mode validation path on 2026-09-02; activation and hardware testing remain pending. NixOS now sets the sole systemd HibernateMode value to shutdown and installs a direct-hibernate-only system-sleep evidence hook. systemd 261.2 replaces the parsed mode list on assignment, writes the configured mode before pre hooks, and aborts before /sys/power/state if that write fails, so there is no platform fallback. The guarded TTY runner enables and verifies pm_debug_messages/pm_print_times, starts a fresh persistent capture, quiesces graphical/audio clients, repeats authoritative root topology/client checks, explicitly selects and verifies [shutdown], and requires HIBERNATE-SHUTDOWN confirmation. Frozen pre/post evidence includes wakeup_sources, pm_wakeup_irq, PCI/graphics state, suspend counters, processes, failed units, and journals. The desktop is restarted only after detached/settled return; otherwise it remains stopped for Hybrid recovery. Bash/shfmt/ShellCheck, Nix formatting/evaluation, and a full host build pass. No lid or ordinary suspend setting was changed. sudo activation is blocked on an interactive password; do not treat this as a completed hibernate test.

The kernel preallocated 12,595,068 KiB, froze devices, disabled CPUs, and entered create_image(), but never reached the 'Writing hibernation image' / swsusp_write path. With no dpm_suspend_end/syscore error logged, this is consistent with the remaining pm_wakeup_pending() branch before in_suspend=1. Wakeup-source counters did not change; 0000:00:01.1 remained zero. pm_wakeup_irq read 7 before kernel entry and no data afterward, so IRQ 7 is not yet attributable. GPP0 Card present/Link Up and NVIDIA enumeration occurred after CPUs/IRQs were restored, making dGPU hotplug a rollback consequence in shutdown mode rather than its trigger. mt7921e 0000:03:00.0 restore timed out with -110 afterward and last_failed_dev records it, but dpm_resume happens after create_image returns and does not cause the pre-image branch. title: Fix legion WMI notify lifetime guard
